newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Sibneft to restructure tax debt by Sept 15.
newsitem.headline: Russian Sibneft to restructure tax debt by Sept 15.

text.p: Russian oil holding company Sibneft has agreed to issue new shares to the government to restructure 1.8 trillion roubles ($310 million) of tax arrears by mid-September, a tax service official said on Wednesday.

The head of the authority for enforcing tax arrears payment, Vladimir Popov, told a news conference the plan had been agreed at a meeting of Sibneft officials, tax service head Alexander Pochinok and First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.
"A decision in principal was taken that by September 15 Sibneft should pay 1.8 trillion roubles by increasing its charter capital," he said.
Popov said 1.8 trillion roubles represented Sibneft's net arrears to the federal budget as of May 1.

A tax service statement said of Sibneft: "To effect a complete end to the question of paying budget arrears of the subsidiaries of this holding we consider it necessary to force the subsidiaries of the holding to carry out restructuring of their financial debts by issuing securities in the form of shares or debt instruments."

It was not clear whether Sibneft itself, or its subsidiaries, which apart from Noyabrskneftegaz include the Omsk Refinery, would issue the new equity. Noyabrskneftegaz owed 1.47 trillion roubles as of May 1.

A government order gives companies with arrears the option of issuing shares or bonds to be held by the government against payment of the arrears. Those which do not restructure or pay their debts will be taken to bankruptcy court, officials say.
Popov said a special government order would approve Sibneft's arrears restructuring programme.
The tax service said total Sibneft debt to all levels of government, including fines, was over six trillion roubles.
